title: Transit-Elnk-Firmware agency registry
description: Tracks agencies with (or requested for) the OPTIONAL second data source and offline static timetable -- see docs/AGENCY_REGISTRY.md. This is not a list of agencies the board works with: live departures via the Transit API already cover most agencies with zero entries here (docs/DEPLOYMENT_OPS.md). An entry only exists for the STA-shaped bonus tier.

$schema.description: Editor-tooling convenience only, pointing back at this file -- not a schema keyword here, just a regular (and permitted) property on the instance document.

id.description: Short, stable, lowercase slug -- used as a filename/identifier once the firmware consumes this registry, so treat it as an API, not a label.

region.description: "City, State/Province, Country" -- enough for a human scanning the list to recognize their own agency.

status.description: requested: someone wants this agency added, no technical fields yet -- see docs/AGENCY_REGISTRY.md's low-friction path. supported: the fields below have been worked out and reviewed, same bar as docs/STA_INTEGRATION.md.

requested_by.description: GitHub username, for a requested entry -- so a contributor picking this up has someone to loop in.

gtfs_static_source.description: Where the static route/stop/trip data actually comes from -- not necessarily the agency's own site (see STA's own entry: its static feed sits behind the same protection as its live one, so this project reads a public GTFS mirror instead).

stop_code_convention.description: What a rider actually has to type into the settings portal to identify a stop for this agency (STA: the numeric code printed on the physical sign).

offline_timetable_supported.description: Whether a pre-generated pack (routes/stops/trips) is built and distributed for this agency's SD-card static-timetable fallback (docs/OFFLINE_AND_BUS_WIFI.md) -- distinct from the live second source, and the thing that actually triggers redistributing a compiled copy of this agency's data to end users. Requires redistribution_permitted: true -- see that field.

docs.description: Path to this agency's own writeup, e.g. docs/STA_INTEGRATION.md -- required for status=supported, same depth (compliance/terms-of-use review included) as that file.

maintainer.description: GitHub username of whoever did the integration work and can answer questions about it.

terms_url.description: The agency's own published terms of use, actually read (docs/STA_INTEGRATION.md's Compliance section is the depth expected) -- not a generic API's usual norms assumed to apply.

redistribution_permitted.description: Whether terms_url's terms permit redistributing a compiled/derived copy of this agency's data to third parties -- a broader ask than fetching it live and displaying it on one device, which is all the live second source (gtfs_rt) does. Required and must be true whenever offline_timetable_supported is true, since building and publishing a pack IS that redistribution. If the terms don't permit it, ship the live second source only and leave offline_timetable_supported false/absent -- don't build a pack.

attribution_required.description: Whether terms_url's terms require an on-device credit (the way Transit's ToS does, docs/DEPLOYMENT_OPS.md -- unlike STA's own terms, which explicitly don't). Required for status=supported so this is a checked fact, not something a future change has to remember to look up.

attribution_text.description: The exact credit text/form required, when attribution_required is true.

redistribution_permitted.description: A pack cannot be built/distributed for this agency unless this is explicitly true -- see this field's own description above.

protocol.description: The only shape the firmware's decoder (sta_feed_parser.h, being generalized) can actually read today. An agency that only offers a OneBusAway-style JSON API instead of raw GTFS-RT protobuf isn't supportable yet -- file it as status=requested with a note, not supported.

auth_header_value.description: Only for a key that's already effectively public (like STA's, published in their own OneBusAway config -- see docs/STA_INTEGRATION.md's Compliance section). Never a private credential -- root CLAUDE.md's rules against committing real keys apply here too.
